Q: Reducing significant digits and eliminating scientific notation when float/double approaches zero A:

"Significant digits" are about formatting, not arithmetic. There's little gain from rounding off intermediate calculations. Think of double as C(++)'s "default" floating-point type, and float as a memory optimization for arrays of millions/billions of numbers when precision doesn't matter.

Q: How to get the ConnectionStatus of a VPN with "Get-VpnConnection" PowerShell command sent with Runtime.exec()? A:

To get connection status from other VPN providers, I have found with Norton VPN, the windows command "ipconfig" lists the following adapter when VPN is connected:

Unknown adapter Norton VPN WireGuard: [the bold is used for matching below]

If VPN is not connected, above adapter is not listed.

Note: My ipconfig also lists "Unknown adapter Norton VPN:" and "Unknown adapter Norton VPN OpenVPN Data Channel Offload:". Do not use these as they are present regardless of connection status.

Other VPN providers may also have their respective adapters behave in similar ways.

So this PS code works for me:

$vpnStatus = if ((& ipconfig) -match "vpn wireguard"){"Online"} else {"Disconnected"}

Q: How should an OIDC client application determine if a user can access UI components? A:

So which one is it?

Practically, I think the IdP would be most likely to introduce a breaking change via updates. I see my language was a bit nebulous here - by "control" I meant to convey that the client and server are our code, and while the IdP will be a third party solution (I'll just come out and say Keycloak), it's able to be configured as we need it and it conforms to OAuth2 and OIDC specs. Sure, these separate components have the capacity to change, but our code can adapt to suit any breaking changes from the third party, e.g. if Keycloak updates or a decision to move to a different hosted IdP happens down the line.

Q: Tkinter Label Class not placing label on window A:

The issue is that you are creating the make_label object but not calling the make_label method which actually creates and places the label you need to call header_label_sl.make_label() after creating the header_label_sl object.

python
 tkinter import * from Classes_File_2503056 import *  main_window = Tk() main_window.title("University Student Information") main_window.geometry("800x400")  header_label_sl = make_label(main_window,                              "Student Login",                              20,                              300,                              10)  header_label_sl.make_label()  # Call the method to create and place the label  main_window.mainloop()

In your original code, you were initializing the make_label object but never actually telling it to create the label widget and place it on the window by adding header_label_sl.make_label(), you're executing the code within the make_label method which creates the Label and uses .place() to put it on the main_window.
